  EVIDENCE: The wrapper passes the workflow name as `check_name` (`workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml:62-65`). The triage script fingerprints by repository, PR, and check name (`scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:144-147`) and exits when an open issue already has that fingerprint (`scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:221-230`). qwen_qwen3_7-plus states the implementation is present and correct, and that the intended behavior is one triage issue per PR per workflow, not per run.
- requirement: “There is one triage per failed run” (README.md:1213-1214, changelog.d/6118-ci-failure-triage-workflow-run.md:9).
  expected_change_site: README.md "Check Failure Triage Phase" trigger wording and/or the changelog table row
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The actual dedup in scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:146,221-231 fingerprints by `REPO|pr=PR_NUMBER|check=CHECK_NAME` and exits when an open issue with that fingerprint exists. For workflow_run triage, `check_name` is the workflow name (workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml:62, .github/workflows/internal-check-failure-triage.yml:50), so repeated failed runs of the same workflow on the same PR while the first triage is open are skipped — they do not each receive a triage. The PR description itself clarifies the design: "the existing dedup keeps one open triage issue per PR and workflow." The implementation matches that design intent (one OPEN issue per PR+workflow, not one per run); the "one triage per failed run" wording in README and the changelog table is imprecise.
